clue.text: Statistics needing to be cooked?

blocks.note: surface reading: figures that someone means to falsify, as in cooking the books
setter's reading: figures not yet processed, so still uncooked like raw food

explanation.surface: An accountant eyes a set of figures that will need fiddling before publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' suggests fraud; the joke is that unprocessed figures are the opposite of cooked, hence raw.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw data are figures gathered but not yet processed or analysed, the uncooked state of statistics.

clue.text: Leader of congregation has time to keep chattering

blocks.note: a rabbi leads a Jewish congregation
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A synagogue leader manages to keep talking during the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of' tempts you to take the first letter of congregation; here the whole phrase means the religious leader.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit, or rabbit on, is to talk at length about trivial things.

clue.text: Irritating complaint from wife a turning point

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
a door turns on its hinge

explanation.surface: A wife's grumbling marks a decisive moment in a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A whinge is a peevish, nagging grumble, a complaint that irritates the hearer.

clue.text: From two countries, original moves meeting silence

indicators.note: when something moves it shifts position, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Novel diplomatic steps from two nations meet a wall of silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglo-Irish describes something relating to both England and Ireland, or to people of mixed descent from both.

clue.text: Try to break into painting's special language

indicators.note: breaking into something gets inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: painting is an art
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Someone urges a novice to get to grips with the jargon of painters.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the slang or jargon of a particular group, a specialised vocabulary.

clue.text: The girl from Lima is reading

blocks.note: Lima is the capital of Peru
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: Someone announces what a young woman from the Peruvian capital is doing: reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'The girl from Lima' as Peru's girl, the country first and then her name.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading through of a document, so the noun matches.

clue.text: Soldier coming down with device to measure boundary

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
a meter is a measuring instrument

explanation.surface: A paratrooper drops in carrying a gauge to survey a perimeter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming down' suits a parachutist, and in a down clue it also means the second piece follows below.
explanation.definitionFit: A parameter is a limiting factor that sets the bounds within which something must operate.

clue.text: River in a bad way — just a brook

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
unwell, poorly

explanation.surface: A river in drought has dwindled to a mere stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a small stream or runnel, smaller even than a brook.

clue.text: Conferences upset MP so? I say!

indicators.note: something upset is knocked out of order, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of MP, so, I and say

explanation.surface: A disgruntled MP at some meetings is greeted with a scandalised exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Symposia is the plural of symposium, a meeting at which experts discuss a subject.

clue.text: A hen will have a fiasco in America

definitions.note: elliptical: what a hen will do

blocks.note: first meaning: what a hen does in the nest
second meaning: American slang for a performance that flops

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a hen disgracing herself in the States; split after 'will' and each half is completed by the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens produce eggs, and in US theatre slang a show that bombs is said to do this.

clue.text: Earnestly ask about home for creature

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes around the second

blocks.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
at home is in

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for a home for an animal, like a rescue appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is any living thing, a creature, as in 'a strange being'.

clue.text: Girl, boy and me horribly coarse and vulgar

indicators.note: something done horribly is botched, so the words before it come out jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of girl, boy and me together

explanation.surface: A girl, a boy and the speaker are accused of being dreadfully crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' sits inside the fodder phrase but adds no letters; it just joins the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides being a Cockney exclamation, gorblimey is used as an adjective for something common, rough and unrefined.

clue.text: Not out having fun? It's early enough

blocks.note: the opposite of out, as a batsman still in
having fun is having a good time

explanation.surface: Someone staying in yet enjoying themselves reassures us there is no rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive in good time means to arrive with time to spare, before the deadline.

clue.text: Shabby, but put on

blocks.note: first meaning: threadbare from much use
second meaning: past participle of wear, as clothes are put on

explanation.surface: A garment is described as tatty yet still being worn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for clothing frayed by use and also the past participle of wear, describing clothes donned.

clue.text: Free gift shared, thinking ahead

indicators.note: set free, the letters break loose from their order

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Passing on a complimentary present shows prudent planning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free gift' reads as a fixed phrase; 'Free' is the instruction and only 'gift shared' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-sighted people plan for the future, anticipating what lies ahead with good judgement.

clue.text: Believe sailor is to get assessment for a loan

blocks.note: to credit a story is to believe it
a rating is an ordinary sailor in the navy

explanation.surface: Someone trusts that a seaman will be scrutinised before borrowing money.
explanation.definitionFit: A credit rating is a lender's judgement of how likely a borrower is to repay.

clue.text: Teacher, give me something to do; I have no idea

blocks.note: a don is a university teacher
to task someone is to set them work

explanation.surface: A bored pupil begs a teacher for work, then claims total ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a casual way of saying one does not know the answer.

clue.text: Piece of fish I dropped: that's done it

blocks.note: a fin is part of a fish
taken as written
to shed is to let fall

explanation.surface: A cook drops a fillet on the floor and declares the meal ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Finished means complete, over and done, the same sense as declaring a job done.

clue.text: Sit diner in mess: grub up!

indicators.note: a mess is disorder, so the letters are put into a jumble

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A soldier is seated in the mess hall and told the food is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub up!' sounds like a call to dinner; read as a verb it means to dig something out of the ground. A mess is a military dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinter is to dig up something buried, just as to grub up is to dig out roots.

clue.text: Characteristic muddling, so I sync diary

indicators.note: muddling things puts them into disorder, so the following letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Someone admits their quirky habit of getting confused, so they synchronise their calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiosyncrasy is a peculiar trait or habit, a characteristic distinctive to one person.

clue.text: Iron Lady's hat

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher, nicknamed the Iron Lady, owns a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' is the famous nickname of Thatcher, but the two words separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a brim and a crown creased lengthwise.

clue.text: Newly design part of train ventilation

indicators.note: a part is only some of the whole, so the letters sit within the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of train and start of ventilation

explanation.surface: An engineer redesigns the air-conditioning system of a train.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent is to devise something new, to design it for the first time.

clue.text: For girl, I almost come to my feet

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
to rise is to stand up

explanation.surface: Someone nearly stands up for a girl, like an old-fashioned gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a girl's name, also a flower and part of the eye.

clue.text: Capacious playing area, topping for some Aussies

blocks.note: roomy, loose-fitting
a green is a grassy area for games, as in a bowling green

explanation.surface: A roomy sports field is described, then said to be the best thing for Australians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like an adjective for excellent; it means something worn on top of the head. The baggy green is the cap worn by Australian Test cricketers.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia's Test cricketers wear a dark green cap, nicknamed for its loose shape: headwear for a select few Australians.

clue.text: Move, sheep! It hauled itself to its feet

blocks.note: to go is to move
a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: A shepherd shouts at a fallen sheep, which then struggles upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Got up is past tense of get up, meaning rose from lying or sitting to standing.

clue.text: Very dangerous to be out on one leg

definitions.text: Very dangerous to be out on one
definitions.note: the answer completes the idiom rather than replacing the phrase

blocks.clueFragment: Very dangerous to be out on one
blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for being in a precarious position
second meaning: an arm or leg

explanation.walkthrough: To be out on a limb is to be exposed and unsupported, like someone on a thin tree branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a branch of a tree in the idiom and also a bodily appendage such as a leg.

clue.text: Success with the gate, so get out

definitions.note: a noun naming a way of getting out, clued by its effect

blocks.note: a hit is a success, as a hit record
a wicket is a small gate, especially one set in a larger door

explanation.surface: Someone triumphs with a gate and is told to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is out hit wicket when they knock over their own stumps with bat or body.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit wicket is one of the cricket dismissals, a mode by which a batsman is given out.

clue.text: People over there start to tamp pipe

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: first letter of tamp
a hose is a flexible pipe

explanation.surface: Those men in the distance begin packing tobacco into a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Those, as a pronoun, points to people further away, as in 'those who wait'.

clue.text: Sturdy rail knocked over in wild duel

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round, so it is read backwards
wild means out of control, so the letters of the following word scatter
in places the first piece within the second

blocks.note: a bar is a rail, as a towel bar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fence gets flattened during a furious fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Durable things last and resist wear, so they are strong and sturdy.

clue.text: Group of whales given a part in online entertainment

blocks.note: a pod is the collective noun for whales
an actor cast in a play is given a role

explanation.surface: A school of whales gets a role in some internet show.
explanation.definitionFit: A podcast is an audio series distributed over the internet for listeners to download or stream.
